events.outcome: Current SK Telecom material establishes the PPS recharge lifecycle, passport onboarding and stay-expiry recharge constraint; current roaming guidance classifies PPS as roaming-unavailable.

data.acquisitionSummary: SK Telecom PPS can be opened by a foreign customer using a valid passport even without an alien registration card; foreign customers are limited to one prepaid line.

keep.action: A KRW5000 voice/SMS recharge gives 30 days outgoing, 40 days incoming and 120 days number retention. The number-retention floor is roughly three KRW5000 actions per 360 days; continuous incoming-SMS availability would require a materially shorter cadence than the 120-day retention window.

data.chinaActivation: A valid passport can open PPS, but passport-opened customers cannot keep recharging after their permitted stay expires without returning to an SKT branch/dealer for identity verification and a limited extension.
data.kyc: Valid passport is accepted without an alien registration card. After stay expiry, further recharge is blocked unless the customer visits an SKT branch/dealer with the passport for identity verification; SKT documents an additional three-month extension path.
data.payment: T world, stores and ARS support PPS recharge. Published card support is Korea-centric; dependable remote foreign-card recharge is not established.
data.roamingSms: SK Telecom current roaming guidance classifies PPS among roaming-unavailable plans. Overseas SMS/OTP reception is therefore not established for this PPS line.
data.holdReason: Passport onboarding is possible, but recharge stops after stay expiry unless identity is re-verified in person, and current SKT roaming guidance classifies PPS as roaming-unavailable; not a clean long-term nonresident OTP route.
data.tariffSummary: KRW5000 gives 30 days outgoing, 40 days incoming and 120 days number retention; passport users face a stay-expiry recharge stop and PPS is classified as roaming-unavailable.
guideSteps: Open PPS in Korea using an accepted identity document such as a valid passport.
Distinguish the 120-day number-retention window from the shorter 40-day incoming-service window.
Do not rely on PPS for long-term overseas OTP unless stay-validity and temporary-roaming requirements are satisfied.
